chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

A man is in his salat (prayer), and a pumpkin seed comes out from him; then there is nothing upon him, and it has not invalidated his wudu (ablution). But if it comes out smeared with feces, then he must repeat the wudu (ablution); and if he is in his salat (prayer), he must break the salat (prayer) and repeat the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer).

key_terms.حَبُّ الْقَرْعِ: a pumpkin seed; an example of a solid object exiting the body
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being performed
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution), the ritual state of purification

ai.seo_question: Does something exiting the body during salat (prayer) invalidate wudu (ablution) and require restarting the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding something exiting the body during salat (prayer). If a dry object exits without being soiled, it does not invalidate wudu (ablution), but if it exits smeared with feces, wudu (ablution) is invalidated and the salat (prayer) must be restarted if one is in it.
